description: Offline literature repository for agentic-openfoam. One entry per cited source across the consultant server (CITATION_SOURCES) and the case reference data. `corpus/references/fetch.py` reads this file and downloads every source that has an open download into corpus/references/cache/ (gitignored) so a user can read the primary sources offline. Copyrighted books and paywalled papers cannot be redistributed; those carry download.method == 'manual' with a DOI/ISBN so the user can obtain them. Keep this manifest in sync with the consultant's CITATION_SOURCES (a test enforces it).

schema.url: canonical reference URL for a human (optional)
schema.consultant_tag: the CITATION_SOURCES key this backs, if any (optional)
schema.used_by: list of consumers (consultant tag / case path)
schema.download: {method: http, url} | {method: foam_src, src} | {method: manual, note}
schema.file: cache filename written by fetch.py (omit for manual)
schema.verified: date the citation/URL was last verified

sources.citation: OpenFOAM v2412 checkMesh defaults: aspectThreshold_=1000, nonOrthThreshold_=70 deg, skewThreshold_=4, in primitiveMeshCheck.C.
OpenFOAM v2412 default mesh-quality controls: maxNonOrtho=65, maxInternalSkewness=4, maxBoundarySkewness=20, maxConcave=80, in etc/caseDicts/meshQualityDict.
OpenFOAM v2412 User Guide, Ch. 4 'Mesh generation and conversion' (mesh-quality controls).
OpenFOAM v2412 User Guide, 6.3 'Solution and algorithm control' (relaxationFactors, residualControl, linear-solver tolerances).

Versteeg, H.K. & Malalasekera, W. (2007). An Introduction to Computational Fluid Dynamics: The Finite Volume Method, 2nd ed. Pearson. Ch. 3 (turbulence & law of the wall), Ch. 5 (convection-diffusion schemes), Ch. 6 (SIMPLE & under-relaxation), Ch. 11 (complex geometries).
